mainTopic: What work is allowed to an אבל and on חול המועד when there is a risk of loss
overview: The משנה discusses a man whose olives were ready for pressing, but mourning, an accident, or workers who did not show up kept him from pressing them before the Festival. רבי יהודה lets him do only the first loading of the press on חול המועד, while רבי יוסי lets him finish the whole job. The גמרא asks why the משנה opens with mourning but rules about the Festival. רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says this shows a mourner may not do work that is allowed on חול המועד. רב אשי instead reads it as two rules: loss-preventing work is allowed during mourning, and even on the מועד. A ברייתא supports רב שישא. It lists urgent jobs that others do for an אבל, when the אבל may work himself, and how different kinds of workers are treated. The גמרא fixes one line of that ברייתא about contract work. The amud ends with a story: מר בריה דרב אחא pulled his ox out of a shared team while mourning. רב אשי objects, and the גמרא explains that an אדם חשוב is stricter with himself.

steps.title: Olives ready for pressing, but the work was delayed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that someone whose olive pressing was delayed may load the press beam once on חול המועד and leave it until after the Festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person turned over his olives to get them ready for pressing. Then mourning, an accident, or workers who did not show up stopped him from pressing them. He may load the beam for the first pressing and leave it until after the Festival. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes a man whose olives were ready to press before the Festival, but something outside his control stopped him. רבי יהודה lets him do a small, limited amount of work on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olives that have been turned over will spoil if they are left sitting, so waiting means a real loss. רבי יהודה allows only the minimum: one loading of the beam, so the olives do not go bad. The rest of the work waits until after the Festival.

keyTerms.meaning: An accident or situation beyond one's control
The workers misled him (they promised to come and did not)
The heavy beam of the olive press
The Festival; here it means חול המועד, the intermediate days

phrases.english: One who turned over his olives
and mourning or an unavoidable accident happened to him
or workers misled him
he may load the beam for the first pressing
and leave it until after the Festival
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda

steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the delay was not his fault, he may load the beam for the first pressing on חול המועד and leave it there until after the Festival.

steps.title: רבי יוסי lets him finish the whole job
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and allows him to finish pressing and seal the barrels the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: he may draw off the oil, finish the job, and seal the barrels the way he normally does.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a second, more lenient opinion in the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allowed only the first step. רבי יוסי allows the entire process, all the way to sealing the barrels. He does not require the man to do the work differently from his usual way, because stopping in the middle could still cause a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Draws off or pours off the oil

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: only the first loading of the beam. רבי יוסי: he may finish everything as usual.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says
he draws off the oil and finishes the job
and seals the barrels in his usual way

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion that disagrees with רבי יהודה in the same case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may finish the whole pressing and seal the barrels normally.

steps.title: Why does the משנה start with mourning and end with the Festival?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the משנה opens with a case of אבל but gives its ruling about the מועד, and asks how the two connect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה began with mourning and ended with the Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out something odd in how the משנה is put together. This sets up the two explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case starts with a mourner, but the ruling is about what he may do on חול המועד. It is not clear what mourning has to do with the Festival. The גמרא wants to know what the link is.

phrases.english: Gemara
It opened with mourning
and ended with the Festival

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about how the משנה is structured
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What connects the mourning at the start of the משנה to the Festival ruling at the end?

steps.title: רב שישא: a mourner may not do what is allowed on the Festival
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי learns from the משנה that work allowed on חול המועד is forbidden during the days of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, said: This teaches that things allowed on חול המועד are forbidden during a person's days of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא answers the question by explaining the link between mourning and the Festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourning happened before the Festival, and it kept him from pressing his olives, because a mourner may not do this work. That is why he was left needing to work on חול המועד. So the משנה teaches that the rules for a mourner are stricter than the rules of the מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: This is to say (this teaches us)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said
This is to say
things that are permitted on the Festival
are forbidden during the days of his mourning

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about how the משנה is structured
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mourning stopped him before the Festival, which shows that work allowed on the מועד is forbidden to a mourner.

steps.title: רב אשי: two separate rules, from the easier case to the harder one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the משנה as a לא מיבעיא statement: work that prevents a loss is obviously allowed during mourning, and it is allowed even on the מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is saying 'it goes without saying.' It goes without saying that this is allowed during the days of mourning, since that ban is only מדרבנן. But even on the Festival, where the ban on work comes from the תורה, the רבנן allowed it when there is a loss.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different explanation of why the משנה mentions both mourning and the Festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not read the משנה as teaching that a mourner is stricter. He says it teaches two rules, going from the easy case to the hard one. The ban on work for a mourner is only מדרבנן, so allowing work there to prevent a loss is simple. The real news is that the רבנן allowed it even on the מועד, where the ban on מלאכה is מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case of financial loss

steps.whatToRemember: רב שישא: the mourning before the Festival is what made him need to work on the מועד, so a mourner is stricter. רב אשי: these are two separate rules, and loss-preventing work is allowed both during mourning and, even more of a חידוש, on the מועד.
steps.confusionAlert: Under רב אשי, the משנה is not saying the mourning happened before the Festival. It is listing two situations, starting with the easier one.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said
it is saying 'it goes without saying'
phrases.notes: He means the משנה starts with the obvious case and then moves to the bigger חידוש.

phrases.english: it goes without saying during the days of his mourning
where it is rabbinic, so it is permitted
but even on the Festival
where the ban on work is from the Torah
in a case of loss
the Rabbis permitted it

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר, לָא מִיבַּעְיָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב שישא's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה teaches two separate rules: loss-preventing work is allowed during mourning, and even on the מועד.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב שישא: others do urgent work for the mourner
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists loss-preventing jobs that others do for an אבל. It suggests the אבל may not do them himself, which supports רב שישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב שישא son of רב אידי: These are the things that people do for a mourner during his days of mourning. If his olives were turned over and are ready, they load them into the press for him. They seal his barrel, lift his flax out of the soaking pool, and lift his wool out of the dye pot. They also water his field when his turn for water comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof for רב שישא's view from Step 4. That view is that work allowed on חול המועד is still forbidden to an אבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says these jobs are done 'for' the אבל, meaning by other people. So even though the work prevents a loss, the אבל himself may not do it. On the מועד, by contrast, a person may do such work himself. That is exactly רב שישא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is in the word 'for him': other people do the work, not the אבל himself.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי.
phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רב שישא son of רב אידי.
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 4: work allowed on the מועד is forbidden during mourning.

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים הָעוֹשִׂין לָאָבֵל בִּימֵי אֶבְלוֹ:
phrases.english: These are the things people do for the mourner during his mourning days:
If his olives were turned over, they load them into the press for him,
and if his barrel needs sealing,
and if his flax needs lifting out of the soaking pool,
and if his wool needs lifting out of the dye pot,
and they water his field
when his turn for the water arrives.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב שישא's reading from Step 4 and backs it up with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב שישא's claim that work allowed on חול המועד is forbidden to an אבל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says others do the loss-preventing work for the אבל, which implies he may not do it himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that mourning is stricter than חול המועד about work, even work that prevents a loss.

steps.title: רבי יהודה adds sowing a field for the mourner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says others may also sow the אבל's plowed field or his flax field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: They may also sow for him a plowed field, or a field set aside for flax.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יהודה adds one more job that others may do for the אבל: sowing his fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה thinks a late planting counts as a loss. So sowing belongs on the list of urgent jobs.

keyTerms.meaning: A plowed field ready for sowing

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף זוֹרְעִין לוֹ
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: They also sow for him
a plowed field, and a field set aside for flax.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף זוֹרְעִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item to the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Others may also sow an אבל's plowed field or flax field.

steps.title: The חכמים reject sowing because it is not a real loss
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה: a field can be planted later or with a different crop, so nothing is truly lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If it is not sown in the early season, it can be sown in the late season. If it is not sown with flax, it can be sown with some other crop.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's addition to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a real, permanent loss allows others to work for the אבל. A delayed planting can be made up later or switched to another crop. So sowing does not qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: From a different kind of crop

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם לֹא תִּזָּרַע בְּבַכִּיר
phrases.english: They said to him: If it is not sown in the early season,
let it be sown in the late season;
if it is not sown with flax,
let it be sown with another kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם לֹא תִּזָּרַע בְּבַכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's addition from Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the addition of sowing to the list.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Late sowing is not a true loss, since it can be done later or with a different crop.
steps.whatToRemember: The test is a real loss. Something that can easily be made up later does not count.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the mourner may work privately if he is the only expert
steps.stepSummary: If only the אבל has the skill to do the urgent job, he may do it himself, quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If his olives were turned over and no expert is there but him, or his barrel needs sealing and no expert is there but him, or his flax must be lifted from the soaking pool or his wool from the dye pot and no expert is there but him, he may do it himself in private.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a case where the אבל himself, not just others, may do the loss-preventing work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally others do these jobs for the אבל. But if nobody else knows how to do them, the loss cannot be avoided any other way. So the אבל may do the work himself, as long as he does it out of public view.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:

phrases.aramaic: זֵיתָיו הֲפוּכִין וְאֵין שָׁם אוּמָּן אֶלָּא הוּא,
phrases.english: If his olives were turned over and there is no expert there but him,

phrases.aramaic: כַּדּוֹ לָגוּף וְאֵין שָׁם אוּמָּן אֶלָּא הוּא,
phrases.english: if his barrel needs sealing and there is no expert there but him,
if his flax needs lifting out of the soaking pool
or his wool out of the dye pot
and there is no expert there but him,
he may do it himself, in private.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's original list and allows the אבל himself to do the work when he is the only expert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When no other expert is available, the אבל may do the loss-preventing work himself, privately.

steps.title: A public craftsman may work before the רגל if no one else can
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further: an אבל who serves the public may work openly before a רגל if he is the only one who can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said even more: If he was a craftsman for the public, or a barber or bath attendant for the public, and the time of the רגל arrived, and there is no expert there but him, he may do the work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a bigger leniency for an אבל whose work serves the whole community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9 the אבל could only work in private to save his own property. Here the public's needs before the רגל are at stake. So he may work without the word 'in private' attached.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels: others may do urgent work for the אבל; he may do it himself privately if he is the only expert; and he may serve the public before a רגל if no one else can.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Going even further, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said:
If he was a craftsman serving the public,
or a barber or bath attendant for the public,
and the time of the Festival arrived,
and there is no expert there but him,
he may do the work.
phrases.notes: Notice that 'in private' is missing here, unlike in the line before.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 9 with a bigger leniency when the public's needs are involved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל who is the only public craftsman, barber or bath attendant may work before a רגל.

steps.title: Farm workers versus drivers and sailors
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says others may work for an אבל who is a tenant farmer, leaser or contractor. Drivers and sailors stop, unless their work was hired out to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tenant farmers, leasers and contractors: others may do their work for them. Donkey drivers, camel drivers and sailors: their work is not done. But if they were leased or hired out to others, the work may be done.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list and sorts mourners by the kind of work they do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Field work for the אבל can be handed to others so his crop is not lost. A driver's or sailor's trip is simply put off, so it stops. If the animal or boat is already hired out to someone else, that other person would lose out, so the work goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: Tenant farmers who work someone's field for a share of the crop
Leasers who pay the owner a fixed amount of crop
Contractors who take on field work for a set price

phrases.english: Tenant farmers, leasers, and contractors:
for these, others may do the work on their behalf.
Donkey drivers, camel drivers, and sailors:
for these, the work is not done,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיוּ מוּחְכָּרִין אוֹ מוּשְׂכָּרִין אֵצֶל אֲחֵרִים —
phrases.english: but if they were leased or hired out to others,
phrases.notes: This means their animals or boats were already rented out to someone else, so the work is really for that other person.

phrases.english: then the work may be done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of loss-preventing work first brought in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Others may do field work for an אבל. A driver's or sailor's work stops, unless it was already hired out to someone else.

steps.title: Day laborer and a job held for others
steps.stepSummary: A day laborer who is an אבל may not work, even in another city. A mourner holding a job for others may not do it, even by contract.
steps.simpleTranslation: A day laborer may not work, even in another city. If he had a job for others in hand, even by contract, he may not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds two more cases where the אבל himself must not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being in another city, where nobody knows he is mourning, does not allow the day laborer to work. The words 'even by contract' will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A day laborer, paid by the day
Contract work, paid for the finished job

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר יוֹם אֲפִילּוּ בְּעִיר אַחֶרֶת — לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: A day laborer, even in a different city, may not work.
If he had work for others in his hands,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבְּקִיבּוֹלֶת — לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: even if it was by contract, he may not do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A day laborer may not work during mourning, and a mourner may not do a job he holds for others.

steps.title: Why would contract work be the bigger חידוש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says 'even by contract', since contract work is the more obvious case to forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Even by contract,' and surely not when it is not by contract?! On the contrary, contract work is like his own work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording 'even by contract' in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even' means the ברייתא thinks contract work is the case where we would most expect him to be allowed. But contract work is paid for the finished job, so it is like his own work and is clearly forbidden. If anything, work paid by time would be the more likely case to allow.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the challenge as saying contract work is allowed. It says contract work is the more obviously forbidden case, so the word 'even' is in the wrong place.

phrases.english: 'Even if it was by contract',
and it goes without saying when it is not by contract?!
On the contrary, contract work is like his own!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבְּקִיבּוֹלֶת, וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא שֶׁאֵינָהּ קִיבּוֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the last line of Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'אף על פי שבקיבולת' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contract work is like the worker's own work, so it is the more obvious case to forbid. It cannot be the 'even' case.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: both kinds are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as forbidding both contract work and work that is not by contract.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: whether by contract or not by contract, he may not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing how we read the ברייתא's phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' is dropped. The ברייתא now simply says the אבל may not do a job held for others, whatever the payment setup.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say this instead (the reading is fixed)

phrases.english: Rather, say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין קִיבּוֹלֶת בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָהּ קִיבּוֹלֶת — לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: whether by contract or not by contract, he may not do it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing how the ברייתא is read (אלא אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא treats contract work as the surprising case to forbid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both contract work and work that is not by contract are forbidden to the אבל.

steps.title: Others doing the אבל's work: his house or elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: If others hold the אבל's job, they may not do it in his house, but they may do it in another house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his work was in the hands of others: in his house they may not do it; in another house they may.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the reverse case: the אבל's own work is being done by other people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the issue is where the work is done. Work done in the mourner's home looks like he is working, so it is forbidden. Somewhere else it is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: A job the אבל holds for others: he may not do it, contract or not. His own job held by others: allowed only outside his house.

phrases.english: If his work was in the hands of others,
in his house, they may not do it;
in another house, they may do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא after the correction in Steps 13 and 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Others may do the אבל's work only outside his house.

steps.title: The shared ox team story
steps.stepSummary: Two partners shared a team of oxen. When one became an אבל, he pulled his ox out of the team.
steps.simpleTranslation: מריון son of רבין and מר son of רב אחא son of רבא shared a team of oxen. A death happened to מר son of רב אחא, and he detached his ox from the team.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up רב אשי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each partner owned one ox in the pair. Once one ox was removed, the team could not work at all, so the partner who was not mourning lost out too.

keyTerms.meaning: A team (pair) of oxen yoked together
Something bad happened to him (a death in the family)

phrases.english: מריון, son of רבין,

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִיּוֹן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִין וּמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case connected to the ברייתא's rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourning partner stopped a shared ox team from working.

steps.title: רב אשי: what about the partner's loss?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges מר: even if he gives up his own profit, the ברייתא allows work that is hired out to others, so he should not cause his partner a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: A great man like מר son of רב אחא does this? Granted he does not care about his own loss, but does he not care about others' loss? Isn't it taught: if they were hired or leased out to others, the work may be done!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי criticizes what מר did and uses the ברייתא from Step 11 against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר may give up his own income, but his partner is not mourning. The ברייתא says work tied to other people goes on, so the partner should have been able to keep working the team.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: רב אשי's point is that the basic law does not require an אבל to stop work that is tied to people who are not mourning. Step 18 explains why מר chose to be stricter anyway.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:

phrases.aramaic: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה כְּמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא עָבֵיד הָכִי?
phrases.english: A great man like מר son of רב אחא acts this way?
Granted that he is not concerned about his own loss,
is he not concerned about that of others?!
But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ מוּשְׂכָּרִין אוֹ מוּחְכָּרִין אֵצֶל אֲחֵרִים —
phrases.english: if they were hired or leased out to others,
phrases.notes: This is the same line from the ברייתא in Step 11, quoted again as proof.

phrases.english: then the work may be done!

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה כְּמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא עָבֵיד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what מר did in Step 16, using the ברייתא from Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בריה דרב אחא's choice to pull his ox out of the shared team.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets work go on when it is tied to others. Stopping the team causes the partner, who is not mourning, a loss he should not suffer.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that מר held an important person must be stricter with himself, so the אבל pulled his ox out even though the basic law might allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he (מר) holds: an important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי's challenge. מר agrees the basic law may allow the ox to keep working, but he holds that an important person must act more strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי argued that the ox should stay in the team, since the ברייתא allows work hired out to others and the partner should not lose money. The answer does not deny that ruling. It adds that an אדם חשוב is held to a higher standard, because people watch him and might learn to treat the laws of אבלות lightly.

keyTerms.meaning: An important person, someone people look up to and learn from
And he holds (this is his view)

steps.whatToRemember: The basic law may permit something, but an אדם חשוב is expected to be stricter so others do not come to take the הלכה lightly.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say the ברייתא is wrong or that hired-out work is forbidden for everyone. The basic law stays the same; only an important person goes beyond it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle found across ש״ס: an אדם חשוב may need to be stricter than the letter of the law, because his behavior teaches others.

phrases.english: And he holds:
phrases.notes: "He" is מר, the one רב אשי was challenging in the last step.

phrases.english: An important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 17 by explaining the conduct in step 16 as extra strictness for an important person.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal-status distinction: the basic law stands, but an important person is stricter with himself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא allows work hired out to others, the אבל had no reason to pull his ox out and cause his partner a loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: The work is technically allowed, but an אדם חשוב acts more strictly so that people do not take the laws of אבלות lightly.
